digest.headline: US inflation acceleration and chip stock declines drove Treasury yields higher as the Nasdaq fell 0.9%.

lede.b: United States inflation, which is the rate at which prices for everyday goods and services rise over time, accelerated again. Federal Reserve officials, who run the central bank that sets monetary policy for the country, signaled tighter policy ahead. This pushed up Treasury yields, which are the interest rates the government pays when it borrows money from investors. The rising yields killed the post-election stock market rally. Chip stocks like Nvidia and AMD also dragged down the Nasdaq index, which is a basket of technology company shares, by 0.9%.
lede.i: US inflation accelerated again, prompting Federal Reserve officials to intensify hawkish signals. Treasury yields jumped and killed the post-election rally across American equities. Concurrently, chip stocks dragged down the Nasdaq by 0.9% after Nvidia and AMD shares sank following an executive exit. AMD shares dove 9%, triggering a broader chip slump in Nasdaq futures after hours.
lede.a: Accelerating US inflation prints triggered hawkish signaling from Federal Reserve officials, driving Treasury yields higher and abruptly terminating the post-election equity rally. Chip equities weighed heavily on the Nasdaq, which fell 0.9% as Nvidia and AMD shares sank following Huang's exit. AMD dropped 9%, transmitting a broader semiconductor slump into after-hours futures.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: FTSE Russell begins US indexes reconstitution

stories.b: The London Stock Exchange group called FTSE Russell starts its semi-annual Russell US indexes reconstitution. An index is a list of certain companies that helps track how a stock market is doing. This process involves updating which companies belong in those lists. The changes happen in December 2026. Market watchers pay attention when companies move in or out of these lists.
stories.i: FTSE Russell starts the December 2026 semi-annual Russell US indexes reconstitution. This procedure adjusts the constituent lists that track specific segments of American equities. Fund managers who track these benchmarks must realign their portfolios to match the updated index membership. The schedule formally commences operations ahead of the final implementation.
stories.a: FTSE Russell initiates the December 2026 semi-annual Russell US indexes reconstitution, driving mandatory rebalancing flows for passive index funds. Arbitrageurs and quantitative funds monitor the reconstitution schedule for inclusion and exclusion anomalies. Implementation dates dictate the execution window for portfolio adjustments across affected US equity baskets.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German shares pause after record streak and JD.com buys retailer

stories.b: The DAX 40 is an index, which is a group of important company stocks tracked together to measure the market. This index slipped slightly by 0.06% to settle at 26,749.95 points. Despite this small dip, the index banked a 3.6% record week after first breaking above 27,000 points. European shares overall finished their best week since June.
stories.i: The DAX slipped 0.06% to 26,749.95 at the close of trade. European shares nonetheless wrapped up their best week since June on strong corporate earnings. The DAX notched a 3.6% gain for the week after crossing the 27,000 threshold for the first time.
stories.a: The DAX retreated 0.06% to 26,749.95, digesting the previous session's milestone break above 27,000. Broad European equities secured their strongest weekly performance since June, driven by robust earnings reports. The index finished the week up 3.6% despite the late-session dip.

stories.b: JD.com is a major Chinese company that sells products online. This company completed a massive takeover of a German appliance retailer. The total value of this deal reached $1.5bn. The acquisition brings the German retailer under the ownership of the Chinese firm.
stories.i: JD.com completed a $1.5bn takeover of a German appliance retailer. The transaction transitions ownership of the domestic appliance seller to the Chinese e-commerce giant. The deal expands foreign corporate presence within the German retail sector.
stories.a: JD.com finalized its $1.5bn acquisition of the German appliance retailer, executing a cross-border consolidation play in the European retail space. The transaction represents a major capital deployment by the Chinese firm into continental consumer markets. The integration will test operational synergies within the domestic appliance sector.

politics.b: European eurozone growth cooled down recently. This slowdown left the German stock market treading water. Bond yields across the eurozone also rose.
politics.i: Eurozone growth cooled during the period, leaving the DAX treading water. Sovereign bond yields across the eurozone pushed higher alongside US counterparts.
politics.a: Cooling macroeconomic data across the eurozone constrained local equity momentum, capping index gains alongside rising sovereign bond yields. Yields across the currency bloc ticked upward in tandem with US debt instruments.

Japan.sub: Japan defense spending, currency levels and corporate property

stories.b: Japan considers spending 60 trillion yen on defense. This money would be spent over the next 5 years. A country's defense budget covers its military forces and equipment. Governments plan these large budgets years in advance. The total reaches 60 trillion yen.
stories.i: Japan eyes 60 trillion yen in defense spending over the next 5 years. This planned fiscal outlay scales up the nation's military budget significantly. Authorities map out these multi-year funding paths to guide procurement and readiness. The total touches 60 trillion yen.
stories.a: Japan eyes 60 trillion yen in defense spending over the next 5 years. This multi-year expenditure trajectory locks in a heavier fiscal burden for military outlays. Analysts evaluate the debt issuance required to fund such sustained procurement expansions. The total expenditure aggregates to 60 trillion yen.

stories.t: Yen Levels and Market Intervention Watch
stories.b: The Japanese currency trades at 159.52 against the dollar and 175.94 against the euro after rebounding from lows. Currency traders watch for possible intervention by authorities. Intervention means government officials buy or sell their own money to change its value. The dollar heads toward its best week in 2 months as the yen weakens toward 160.
stories.i: The yen trades at 159.52 against the dollar and 175.94 against the euro following a rebound from earlier lows. Market participants monitor potential intervention by authorities to correct currency weakness. The dollar tracks toward its strongest week in 2 months as the yen weakens toward 160.
stories.a: The yen trades at 159.52 against the dollar and 175.94 against the euro after recovering from cyclical troughs. Traders price in residual tail risk regarding intervention by authorities to arrest currency depreciation. The dollar secures its strongest weekly performance in 2 months while the yen drifts toward 160.

stories.b: Wacoal Holdings plans to sell the Kojimachi Building in a deal worth tens of billions of yen. A famous architect named Kisho Kurokawa designed this building. The sale accelerates the company's asset-light strategy. An asset-light strategy means selling physical property to focus on core business operations.
stories.i: Wacoal Holdings prepares to sell the Kisho Kurokawa-designed Kojimachi Building in a transaction worth tens of billions of yen. This divestment accelerates the firm's asset-light strategy. Corporate restructuring initiatives of this type reduce property holdings to streamline balance sheets.
stories.a: Wacoal Holdings executes the sale of the Kisho Kurokawa-designed Kojimachi Building for tens of billions of yen. This transaction accelerates the corporate asset-light strategy by monetising non-core real estate. Balance sheet optimisation through property divestments allows redeployment into core operational segments.

India.label: India
India.sub: Indian markets see index gains, rupee moves, and debt sales

stories.t: Stock Indices Rise and Currency Slips
stories.src: HDFC Sky · Business Standard · Reserve Bank of India
stories.b: The Sensex and Nifty share indices went up for the third week in a row. Share indices are groups of company stocks tracked together to measure the market. Foreign institutional investors, which are big overseas investment funds, drove these gains by buying shares. Meanwhile, the Indian rupee fell 0.3% to 94.24 against the US dollar over the week. The rupee is the official money used in India.
stories.i: The Sensex and Nifty posted their third consecutive weekly advance, aided by purchases from foreign institutional investors. Concurrently, the rupee depreciated to 94.24 against the US dollar. Rising crude prices further pressured the currency, weakening it to 94.25 per dollar while pushing up the benchmark 10-year bond yield.
stories.a: Equities extended their winning streak to a third week on persistent inflows from foreign institutional investors. Macroeconomic headwinds surfaced as crude oil prices surged, dragging the local currency down to 94.25 against the greenback and driving the 10-year sovereign yield higher. The current account deficit widened to $7.4bn in September, up from $5.2bn in the same month of the previous year.

stories.t: State and Central Debt Auctions Announced
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled auctions for state government securities and treasury bills. State governments offered to sell stock worth ₹23,300 crore in total face value. The central bank also announced treasury bill auctions worth ₹23,000 crore across three different tenors. Treasury bills are short-term loans made to the government that pay back money after a set period.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled debt auctions covering both state government securities and federal treasury bills. State governments offered an aggregate ₹23,300 crore in stock via price-based auctions. Simultaneously, the central bank announced a ₹23,000 crore treasury bill issuance split across 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day tenors for settlement on November 19, 2026.
stories.a: State administrations offered ₹23,300 crore of securities through re-issues and new auctions managed by the Reserve Bank of India. The central bank complemented these state-level borrowings with a ₹23,000 crore treasury bill auction scheduled across 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day maturities. Settlement for these short-term instruments is slated for November 19, 2026.

politics.b: No political updates were reported in the financial sources for India today.
politics.i: No political developments were detailed in the economic reports for India.
politics.a: No political risk factors or governmental policy shifts were cited in the financial releases.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras acquisitions, discoveries and currency pressure

stories.t: Petrobras Buys Logum Stake and Makes Amapa Discovery
stories.b: Petrobras bought a 70% stake in Logum for 620m reals. Logum moves ethanol through pipelines. Petrobras also found a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa. The company faced a new arbitration case from a unit of Seatrium over 55.7m US dollars.
stories.i: Petrobras acquired a 70% stake in Logum for R$620m to expand its logistics footprint. The state-controlled producer added a fresh offshore oil discovery off the Amapa coast to its portfolio. Meanwhile, a unit of Seatrium initiated arbitration proceedings against Petrobras regarding 55.7m US dollars.
stories.a: Petrobras executed the acquisition of a 70% interest in Logum for R$620m while concurrently expanding its exploratory asset base via an oil discovery off Amapa. Concurrently, operational friction surfaced as a Seatrium unit filed a 55.7m US dollars arbitration claim against the energy conglomerate.

stories.t: Brazilian Real Weakness Hits Coffee and Markets React to Fiscal Concerns
stories.b: The Brazilian real tumbled, which weighed on coffee prices as early gains were erased. The Ibovespa index gained 0.66% to reach 172,457.76 points on Friday. Fiscal concerns met earnings support during the trading sessions.
stories.i: A weakening Brazilian real put downward pressure on soft commodities, causing coffee prices to erase earlier gains. Broad market sentiment remained resilient as the Ibovespa index rose 0.66% to close at 172,457.76 points on Friday, balancing fiscal concerns against corporate earnings support.
stories.a: Depreciation in the Brazilian real acted as a transmission mechanism deflating local agricultural valuations, forcing coffee futures to relinquish initial gains. Simultaneously, the Ibovespa advanced 0.66% to 172,457.76 points on Friday as positive corporate earnings outweighed prevailing fiscal anxiety.

politics.b: Brazil manages its economy through central bank interest rate decisions and state-owned corporate strategies. The currency value fluctuates against foreign money like the euro. Government fiscal choices directly affect local stock exchanges and commodity markets.
politics.i: Monetary policy decisions, specifically regarding the Selic rate, anchor macroeconomic conditions and dictate currency pairs like EUR/BRL. State-directed entities such as Petrobras drive significant capital expenditure and M&A activity. Fiscal policy discussions continue to generate volatility across domestic equities.
politics.a: Policy transmission relies heavily on the central bank's Selic rate path, which anchors the trajectory of the real against major crosses like the euro. State-capital allocation via Petrobras shapes domestic industrial consolidation and energy output metrics. Concurrently, fiscal sustainability debates constrain equity valuation multiples on the Ibovespa.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Oil production, pipeline expansions, and regional security

stories.b: OPEC+ is a big group of countries that work together to control how much oil they pump out. This group increased its oil output by 2.04 million barrels per day in October. Iraq pushed its oil production to the highest level since 2019. Saudi Arabia cut its Arab Light crude official selling prices for Asia by the largest drop in over two decades.
stories.i: OPEC+ raised its collective oil output by 2.04 million barrels per day in October. Iraq drove part of this volume by running above its production target to hit its highest level since 2019 according to the IEA. Saudi Aramco responded to shifting market conditions by implementing the largest price cut for its Arab Light crude to Asia in over twenty years.
stories.a: The broader OPEC+ coalition expanded output by 2.04 million barrels per day in October, coinciding with Iraqi production breaching quota limits to reach peaks not seen since 2019 per IEA tracking. Saudi Aramco initiated a deep reduction in its official selling price for Arab Light to Asian buyers, marking the sharpest contraction in over two decades as supply dynamics shift.

stories.b: Aramco is exploring the expansion of its East-West Pipeline to avoid the Hormuz route. A ministry confirmed an attempted drone attack targeted a Saudi Aramco building in Riyadh. Meanwhile, Aramco Trading sold Khafji crude cargoes to Chinese and South Korean refineries.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco is investigating the expansion of its East-West Pipeline as an alternative transit route avoiding Hormuz. The energy ministry confirmed an attempted drone attack targeted a Saudi Aramco facility in Riyadh. On the commercial side, Aramco Trading placed Khafji crude shipments with buyers in Chinese and South Korean refineries.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco is actively studying the capacity expansion of the East-West Pipeline to mitigate transit bottlenecks around Hormuz. State authorities confirmed an interception following an attempted drone attack targeting a Saudi Aramco installation in Riyadh. Concurrently, Aramco Trading executed crude placement transactions for Khafji grades directly with end-users in Chinese and South Korean refining facilities.

politics.b: The UAE exited OPEC, drawing a welcome from Donald Trump and giving the UAE the ability to speed up oil investments. China is gaining regional influence as OPEC+ loses market sway during the Iran war. Meanwhile, PSQL stock backed by Aramco and Google Cloud trades at $4.
politics.i: The UAE departed OPEC, receiving explicit praise from Donald Trump while securing freedom to accelerate capital investments. Concurrently, broader regional dynamics shifted as OPEC+ lost market sway amidst the Iran conflict while Chinese influence expanded. In corporate markets, the Aramco and Google Cloud backed PSQL stock traded at $4.
politics.a: The official exit of the UAE from OPEC drew endorsement from Donald Trump, unlocking accelerated investment pathways for the producer outside formal quotas. Regional market structures experienced structural shifts as OPEC+ lost aggregate pricing power during the Iran conflict, allowing China to expand its footprint. Meanwhile, equity valuation for the Google Cloud and Aramco-backed PSQL held at $4 per share.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Exchange rates and corporate payouts in Nigeria

stories.b: The Nigerian currency, the naira, traded at a rate of N1,353 per US dollar in the official market. In the parallel market, which is an unofficial alternative marketplace for exchanging currencies, the rate reached N1,408 per dollar. Exchange rates show how much of one currency is needed to buy another. These numbers reveal the differing costs of acquiring foreign money through official channels versus alternative ones. The naira closed at N1,353 per US dollar.
stories.i: The naira recorded N1,353 per US dollar within the official forex market. Meanwhile, the parallel market priced the currency at N1,408 per dollar. These divergent rates illustrate the persistent spread between official trading platforms and unofficial channels. Liquidity constraints continue to drive activity across both segments. The naira closed at N1,353 per US dollar.
stories.a: Spot pricing for the naira registered at N1,353 per US dollar in the official forex venue, contrasted with N1,408 per dollar in parallel trading. This dual-rate structure underscores ongoing fragmentation in foreign exchange allocation and liquidity depth. Arbitrageurs monitor the persistent wedge between official matching engines and street-level desks. The naira closed at N1,353 per US dollar.

Dividends are regular payments made by a company to its owners out of its earnings. This increase gives investors a higher return for each share they hold. The naira dividend reached N258 per share.
stories.i: Seplat Energy enhanced its third-quarter shareholder remuneration by lifting its payout. The naira dividend reached N258 per share. Corporate distributions of this nature reflect underlying cash flow generation during the period. Shareholders receive this cash return relative to their equity holdings. The naira dividend reached N258 per share.
stories.a: Seplat Energy augmented its third-quarter shareholder distribution, expanding cash returns to equity owners. The naira dividend reached N258 per share. Such distribution adjustments signal management's confidence in near-term liquidity and operational cash conversion cycles. Investors benchmark these yields against prevailing fixed-income alternatives. The naira dividend reached N258 per share.

Australia.sub: Australian dollar declines and mining stocks update

stories.t: Australian Dollar Slides Against Major Currencies
stories.b: The money used in Australia, called the Australian dollar, fell by 3% in value compared to the United States dollar. This big drop puts the currency near the edge of its normal trading limits. Traders kept selling the currency over several sessions. The Australian money also dropped against the Indonesian rupiah and the Thai baht. Persistent selling pressure drove the downward movement across these currency pairs.
stories.i: The Australian dollar dropped by 3% against its US counterpart, pushing the exchange rate toward the lower boundary of its multi-month range. Persistent selling pressure also drove the AUD/USD pair down. Similar weakness appeared in the carry trade as the currency drifted lower against the Indonesian rupiah and Thai baht. Traders maintained aggressive short positions through these sessions. Heavy selling dominated the foreign exchange flow.
stories.a: The AUD/USD exchange rate retreated 3%, threatening a decisive break of the multi-month consolidation range. Unrelenting selling pressure expanded beyond the greenback to regional crosses, pushing the currency lower against the Indonesian rupiah and Thai baht. Momentum traders capitalized on the breach of local technical supports. Persistent liquidation dominated order books across multiple pairs.

Market analysts evaluated whether these valuations reflected sustainable operational margins. Construction sector equities on the Australian exchange also drew renewed technical interest. Investors reassessed risk premiums across the local resource sector.

Fundamental analysts scrutinized the earnings multiples to determine if the price appreciation outpaced underlying cash flows. Construction-related listings on the ASX similarly registered increased bullish participation. Price discovery continued to challenge consensus models across domestic resource names.
